questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the first of the four tests a real asset must pass?
options: It must appear in a press release
It must be used by every department
It has an identifiable, named owner
It must be stored in a cloud database
questions.explain: The four tests are ownership, measurable value, active maintenance, and being weighed in decisions — ownership is the first.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say most company data fails the 'measurable value' test?
options: Measurable value only applies to physical buildings
Accounting standards forbid valuing data at all
Data has no value under any circumstances
Few organizations can say what a dataset is worth or what it costs to lose, corrupt, or lack it
questions.explain: Unlike a warehouse with a known value and loss cost, most organizations can't price what a dataset is worth or what a bad version of it actually costs.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as a real obstacle to treating data as an asset — not just an excuse?
options: Only large companies produce data
Data cannot be owned by any individual by law
Data never changes once it's created
Data's value is contextual — valuable in one use case, worthless in another
questions.explain: The lesson names three real obstacles: intangibility, distributed creation, and contextual value — not legal or technical impossibility.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what typically happens to organizational data that isn't actively maintained?
options: It gets deleted by default after one year
It becomes more valuable the older it gets
It automatically improves over time
It decays — fields go stale and definitions drift until a report looks wrong
questions.explain: Unmaintained data decays quietly — the opposite of a physical asset that's inspected and serviced on a schedule.

questions.q: What does the lesson say becomes routine when an organization genuinely treats data as an asset?
options: Only the IT department is allowed to touch data
Named ownership, measured quality, and data considered explicitly before systems are retired
All data gets deleted to reduce liability
Data stops being stored in spreadsheets entirely
questions.explain: The lesson names three concrete changes: named owners, measured/reported quality, and explicit consideration of data before systems or teams change.
